terms.gloss: a profession, an art (medicine, law, teaching)
evidence: Lewis & Short, s.v. ars: “a profession, art”
terms.comment: The skill one practises and lives by; Cicero sets the arts that call for learning, medicine, architecture and teaching, above the trades of the workshop.

evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.21: professiō bene dīcendī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: First a public declaration (of one’s name, property, intentions), then the calling one declares: oratory, the teaching of grammar. Mostly post-Augustan.

phrases.latin: quibus autem artibus aut prūdentia major inest aut nōn mediocris ūtilitās quaeritur, ut medicīna, ut architectūra, ut doctrīna rērum honestārum, hae sunt iīs, quōrum ōrdinī conveniunt, honestae
phrases.english: but the professions that call for more wisdom or bring no small benefit, such as medicine, architecture and the teaching of honourable things, are honourable for those whose station they suit

sources: Lewis & Short: ars · Lewis & Short: professio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 365.
